title: Nvidia earnings: Wall Street hopes for a fresh boost for the AI trade
byline: Tom Carter, Jennifer Sor, Max Adams
excerpt: Investors wants clarity on the strength of AI demand, with NVDA stock up 14% YTD. The call with analysts will begin at 5 p.m. ET.
content_html:
Live Updated 2026-08-26T17:05:47.756Z

Nvidia earnings: Wall Street hopes the chip titan can keep carrying the AI trade, with the stock up 14% in 2026

Read in app

Nvidia will have the final word on the AI trade this earnings season.

The tech titan is about to deliver its results for the second quarter, and the stakes are high. After a bout of volatility sent many high-flying AI stocks tumbling this summer — causing a hedge fund meltdown in the process — investors are eager for a bullish catalyst to get the party started again.

But the bar is high, and the stock isn't the driver of market gains the way it once was. Nvidia shares are up 14% this year, eclipsed by bigger rallies among other chip makers.

Still, it remains the leader in AI-enabling chip tech, and investors expect another quarter of red-hot growth. Investors will listen for details on the ramp of its next-gen Vera Rubin chip, clarity on vendor financing and its growing web of deals with other tech firms, and implications of open-source models for Nvidia's total addressable market.

The results will be published shortly after 4 p.m. ET. The call with analysts will begin at 5 p.m. ET.

Copied!

A hyperscaler headache

Some of Nvidia's biggest customers are struggling to out-earn their AI spending. Google reported a negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in Q2, while Amazon's free cash flow fell to a $7.6 billion outflow for the 12 months ending in June. Meta's free cash flow plunged 91% from the previous year. Given that these companies buy Nvidia's chips for internal use and to rent them to their own customers, having less cash is potentially a problem for Nvidia.

On top of that, Google and Amazon are firing up their own competing chip businesses. Google said it delivered its first TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) to customer data centers in Q2, and Amazon said it is also in discussions to sell its Trainium chips directly. Nvidia said in November that it was "delighted" by Google's success — but are Nvidia's investors?

Copied!

BofA says Nvidia remains a 'top sector pick'

BofA says Nvidia is a top pick in semiconductors, and pointed to five things investors should focus on heading into the earnings call:

  1. The launch and supply of Vera Rubin, and if there are changes to Nvidia's forecast that it can generate more than $1 trillion in revenue from 2025 to 2027
  2. Clarity on vendor financing and backstops in Nvidia's deal with OpenAI, and when cash can shift to buybacks
  3. Whether Nvidia can maintain gross margins despite memory cost inflation
  4. How fast demand is growing among hyperscalers and the accelerated-computing infrastructure and enterprise-related firms Nvidia works with
  5. If open-source AI models become more popular relative to closed models, and the implications that could have on Nvidia's addressable market.

The bank reiterated its "buy" rating and its $350 price target for the stock, implying 64% upside from current levels.

Copied!

Nvidia's cash cow vs AI uncertainty

Nvidia's tangled web of AI deals is fuelling investor uncertainty around the broader AI industry, but that is unlikely to stop the company from posting another round of blockbuster earnings.

Naveen Chhabra, a principal analyst at Forrester, said that despite all the headwinds buffeting the AI industry, Nvidia was still expected to announce a record-breaking quarter as it pursues a $1 trillion order book through 2027.

Naveen Chhabra, a principal analyst at Forrester, said that despite all the headwinds buffeting the AI industry, Nvidia was still expected to announce a record-breaking quarter as it pursues a $1 trillion order book through 2027.

Its earnings will be a "battle between jaw-dropping margins and the broader macroeconomic anxiety over when AI spending will break its own records by a big margin," Chhabra said.

Copied!

Details on customer financing, Rubin could be catalysts, GS says

Goldman analysts said they expected Nvidia to "deliver solid results" for the second quarter and issue guidance "well-above" consensus estimates for the following three-month period, largely due to the boom in datacenters and expectations for Nvidia to begin its Rubin ramp in the third quarter.

The bank added that it expects earnings per share to come in at around 6% above consensus estimates for the second quarter, and 12% above estimates for the third quarter.

Goldman analysts said they expected Nvidia to "deliver solid results" for the second quarter and issue guidance "well-above" consensus estimates for the following three-month period, largely due to the boom in datacenters and expectations for Nvidia to begin its Rubin ramp in the third quarter.

The bank added that it expects earnings per share to come in at around 6% above consensus estimates for the second quarter, and 12% above estimates for the third quarter.

Analysts also listed several talking points likely to move Nvidia stock, with details on the company's $500 billion customer financing platform and the Rubin ramp at the top of the list.

The focus among investors will also likely be centered on issues like AI monetization and the return on investment among hyperscalers, and whether Nvidia can maintain its gross margins, it added.

The bank reiterated its "buy" rating and $285 price target, implying 33% upside.

Copied!

JPMorgan flags what could move the stock

JPMorgan analysts are anticipating Nvidia to beat on earnings and lift guidance for the current quarter. The bank said it expects revenue to come in at around $94 billion to $95 billion, a 15% increase from the first quarter.

Analysts said Nvidia's stock was unlikely to see a strong trading day, pointing to historical drops following its past earnings reports. Analysts said shares would be more likely to move based on these topics that could come up on the call:

But the bar is high, and the stock isn't the driver of market gains the way it once was. Nvidia shares are up 14% this year, eclipsed by bigger rallies among other chip makers.

Still, it remains the leader in AI-enabling chip tech, and investors expect another quarter of red-hot growth. Investors will listen for details on the ramp of its next-gen Vera Rubin chip, clarity on vendor financing and its growing web of deals with other tech firms, and implications of open-source models for Nvidia's total addressable market.

A hyperscaler headache

Some of Nvidia's biggest customers are struggling to out-earn their AI spending. Google reported a negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in Q2, while Amazon's free cash flow fell to a $7.6 billion outflow for the 12 months ending in June. Meta's free cash flow plunged 91% from the previous year. Given that these companies buy Nvidia's chips for internal use and to rent them to their own customers, having less cash is potentially a problem for Nvidia.

On top of that, Google and Amazon are firing up their own competing chip businesses. Google said it delivered its first TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) to customer data centers in Q2, and Amazon said it is also in discussions to sell its Trainium chips directly. Nvidia said in November that it was "delighted" by Google's success — but are Nvidia's investors?

BofA says Nvidia remains a 'top sector pick'

BofA says Nvidia is a top pick in semiconductors, and pointed to five things investors should focus on heading into the earnings call:

  1. The launch and supply of Vera Rubin, and if there are changes to Nvidia's forecast that it can generate more than $1 trillion in revenue from 2025 to 2027
  2. Clarity on vendor financing and backstops in Nvidia's deal with OpenAI, and when cash can shift to buybacks
  3. Whether Nvidia can maintain gross margins despite memory cost inflation
  4. How fast demand is growing among hyperscalers and the accelerated-computing infrastructure and enterprise-related firms Nvidia works with
  5. If open-source AI models become more popular relative to closed models, and the implications that could have on Nvidia's addressable market.

The bank reiterated its "buy" rating and its $350 price target for the stock, implying 64% upside from current levels.

Nvidia's cash cow vs AI uncertainty

Nvidia's tangled web of AI deals is fuelling investor uncertainty around the broader AI industry, but that is unlikely to stop the company from posting another round of blockbuster earnings.

Naveen Chhabra, a principal analyst at Forrester, said that despite all the headwinds buffeting the AI industry, Nvidia was still expected to announce a record-breaking quarter as it pursues a $1 trillion order book through 2027.
